metaDescription: Six Energy Star dehumidifiers compared by certification tier, stated energy savings, noise and pint rating, with the efficiency math behind running cost.
expertTake: The Uthfy 38 pint Energy Star Most Efficient is the pick for most damp homes because it combines the top efficiency tier with a mid-size rating. The Ludatido 80 pint at 35 dB is the pick for a big, wet space that you also live in. Buyers who run a dehumidifier only a few weeks a year can skip the efficiency premium and buy any certified unit.
introParagraphs: Energy Star on a dehumidifier is a measurement, not a slogan. The program rates how many liters of water a machine removes for each kilowatt hour it uses, and it certifies only models that beat a threshold. The top tier, Most Efficient, is reserved for the best performers.

The practical benefit shows up over time. A dehumidifier that runs for hours every day through a damp season turns a small efficiency gap into a measurable difference on the bill. How much that matters depends on how long you run it, so the first question is your own hours, not the logo.

products.name: Uthfy 38 Pint Energy Star Most Efficient 2025 Dehumidifier
products.description:
Uthfy carries the Most Efficient designation, the top of the Energy Star program, on a 38 pint compressor machine. That tier goes only to a small slice of certified models, so it marks a real engineering edge in water removed per kilowatt hour. For a home that runs a dehumidifier most of the summer, it is the label that pays back most.

The 38 pint rating sits in a useful middle: large enough for a damp basement of 2,000 to 3,000 square feet, but not so large that the machine is always oversized. Three modes cover everyday control, quiet sleep running and a continuous setting for wet days. Dual drainage lets you use the tank or a hose.

Against the Midea 22 pint, it has far more capacity and the higher tier. Wash the filter every few weeks, run the hose to a drain and set the target near 45 to 50 percent. It is the best balance of efficiency and capacity here.
products.bestFor: A damp 2,000 to 3,000 sq ft space that runs for months.
pros: 38 pints suits a mid-size damp home

products.name: Ludatido 2026 Upgraded 80 Pint Energy Star Dehumidifier, 35 dB
products.description:
Ludatido pairs a large 80 pint capacity with a 35 dB listing, a combination that usually forces a compromise. The listing attributes the quiet to a mute compressor and an upgraded fan structure, and it carries Energy Star certification. A machine that is quiet at this size can sit in a finished basement without becoming a nuisance.

The 1.32 gallon tank is generous and will last through several damp days if you do not use a hose. The 5,000 square foot coverage claim leaves ample margin for a big house. Against the Uthfy, it has more than twice the capacity and a lower noise listing, but it carries a standard certification rather than the Most Efficient tier.

Leave space between the case and the walls, check the hose, and rinse the filter as it clogs. A large, wet space that you also live or work in is its natural territory.
products.bestFor: A large, wet finished basement where noise matters.
pros: 35 dB listing on an 80 pint unit
5,000 sq ft margin for large homes
cons: Standard tier rather than Most Efficient
Oversized for a small damp room
Brand with a short service record

products.name: AEOCKY 74 Pint Energy Star Version 6.0 Dehumidifier, 5,000 sq ft
products.description:
AEOCKY states two outputs, 74 pints at 95 degrees and 95 percent humidity and 52 pints at 86 degrees and 80 percent. The second figure, a warm damp basement, is closer to the conditions where an efficiency rating matters. A machine that removes 52 pints in a damp basement and uses less energy per pint is the combination an Energy Star buyer is looking for.

The listing is blunt about what it calls marketing, and the claims are worth reading with the same skepticism you would apply to any listing. What stands out is the stated damp-basement number, which most rivals leave out. Against the Ludatido, it lists less capacity but gives a realistic figure.

Set a target near 50 percent, run the hose, and rinse the filter every few weeks. It is a solid pick for a large damp basement where efficiency and a stated real-world rating matter.
products.bestFor: A large damp basement where a stated real-world output matters.
pros: States output at a damp-basement condition
cons: Aggressive marketing language in the listing

products.name: DREO 75 Pint Energy Star 2025 Smart Dehumidifier, 1.85 Gal Tank

specList.label: Efficiency
specList.value: Energy Star 2025, 30 percent less energy per listing

products.description:
DREO's listing quantifies its efficiency: Energy Star 2025 certification and a claim of 30 percent less energy than a standard unit. The number is a comparison against a baseline model, so treat it as a marketing figure, but it points the same direction as the certification. A 75 pint capacity and a 41 dB noise level round out a large, fairly quiet machine.

The 1.85 gallon tank is the largest in this guide, so a hose is optional in many homes. Smart app control adds scheduling, which lets you run the unit during off-peak electricity hours where rates vary. Against the Ludatido, it has a larger tank and an app but a slightly higher noise figure.

Confirm that the on-unit humidistat works without the app, keep the hose clear, and wash the filter when needed. In a big basement, the scheduling and large tank both earn their place.
products.bestFor: A large basement where scheduling and a big tank are useful.
pros: Energy Star 2025 with a stated 30 percent saving
cons: Energy claim is against a baseline

products.name: Glowells 52 Pint Energy Star Dehumidifier with Intelligent Control
products.description:
Glowells offers a 52 pint Energy Star machine with a chip that detects humidity and holds a target. A control chip is useful for efficiency because it lets the machine cycle off as soon as the room is at target. Three modes include DEHU, the standard everyday setting.

The 4,500 square foot coverage is the generous kind of claim. Against the Uthfy, it has more capacity but no Most Efficient tier. Against the Midea, it has more than twice the rating and a larger case.

A central spot and a clear hose are the main setup points, with a filter rinse as dust builds. It is a reasonable mid-size choice for a basement of about 2,000 to 3,000 square feet.
products.bestFor: A mid-size basement that wants a certified unit with automatic control.

products.name: Midea 22 Pint Energy Star Dehumidifier, 31 Percent Energy Saving

specList.label: Efficiency
specList.value: Energy Star, saves 31 percent per listing

products.description:
Midea's 22 pint unit is the small, well-known Energy Star option, and the listing states it saves 31 percent energy compared with traditional units. As with the DREO's figure, that is a comparison to a baseline, but the certification behind it is real. A smaller machine costs less to run in absolute terms, which is the simplest efficiency of all.

It is rated for 1,500 square feet, so it suits a moderately damp lower level. At 47 dBA it is audible but acceptable. Against the Uthfy, it has much less capacity and lacks the Most Efficient tier, but it is lighter and cheaper to buy.

Vacuum the coil yearly, leave clearance around the case, and wash the filter when it clogs. Choose it for a smaller space where a big machine would be wasted.
products.bestFor: A moderately damp 1,000 to 1,500 sq ft space.
pros: Energy Star with a stated 31 percent saving
cons: Less capacity than the larger units

buyingCriteria.explanation: Energy Star certification means a model beats a minimum efficiency threshold, usually measured in liters of water per kilowatt hour. Most Efficient is a higher tier for the best performers, and the Uthfy carries it. If the machine runs a few weeks a year the difference is trivial, and over a long season it adds up. Check the tier against the model year too, since the program updates its criteria and a 2025 or 2026 designation reflects the current bar rather than an older one.

buyingCriteria.criterion: How many hours you actually run it
buyingCriteria.explanation: A 300 watt machine running eight hours a day for 120 days uses about 288 kilowatt hours. A 10 percent efficiency gain saves roughly 29 of those, which is small for a short season and noticeable over two or three. Estimate your hours before paying any efficiency premium. A simple way is to count the damp weeks in your climate and multiply by the hours the machine cycles on each day, then compare that to the premium you would pay for the top tier.

The DREO claims 30 percent less energy and the Midea claims 31 percent, both against a traditional unit. Those figures depend on what baseline the maker chose. Treat them as direction, and rely on the certification tier for comparison. A percentage saving also says nothing about how much water the machine removes, so a high saving on a tiny unit can still cost more to run than a modest saving on a right-sized one.

A large machine in a small room reaches target and cycles off quickly, which is efficient. A machine that is too small runs nonstop and still falls short. The Midea at 22 pints fits a 1,500 square foot space, and the Ludatido at 80 pints fits a whole house.

A humidistat that shuts the machine off at target saves more than any badge. The Glowells uses a chip for intelligent control and the Uthfy has an auto mode. Avoid running a unit continuously once the room is dry. Continuous mode is meant for a drying push after a flood or a wet weekend, not for every day, and leaving it on wastes the efficiency you paid for.

An efficient machine that you switch off because it is loud saves nothing. The Ludatido lists 35 dB and the DREO lists 41 dB with a 1.85 gallon tank. Check noise and drain route as seriously as the label.

specDecoder.meaning: The Energy Star measure of water removed per unit of energy. Higher is better, and about 1.6 or more is typical of certified models.
specDecoder.watchFor: Few listings state it, so rely on the tier: certified or Most Efficient.

howWeEvaluated.title: Certification tier
howWeEvaluated.description: We separated Most Efficient from standard certified models. The Uthfy's Most Efficient 2025 tier led, with the rest in standard certified. Claims without a stated tier ranked lower.

howWeEvaluated.title: Realistic output
howWeEvaluated.description: We favored ratings tied to damp conditions, such as the AEOCKY's 52 pints at 86 degrees and 80 percent. Maximums at 95 degrees were treated as ceilings. Capacity was judged against likely room sizes.

howWeEvaluated.title: Savings claims
howWeEvaluated.description: We read stated savings such as the DREO's 30 percent and the Midea's 31 percent as directional. Baselines are chosen by the maker. We weighted certification over percentage claims.

howWeEvaluated.title: Control and cycling
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked for humidistats, auto modes and chips that cycle the machine off at target. The Glowells and Uthfy stood out. Continuous-only designs ranked lower.

howWeEvaluated.title: Noise and drainage
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared noise listings and tank sizes, from 1.32 gal on the Ludatido to 1.85 gal on the DREO. A quiet, easy-to-drain machine stays on. Owner feedback patterns informed the order.

cards.label: Most Efficient
cards.text: The Uthfy carries the top Energy Star tier. It removes more water per kilowatt hour and pays back over a long season. It costs a little more up front.

cards.label: Certified
cards.text: The Ludatido, AEOCKY, DREO, Glowells and Midea meet the standard threshold. They cost less and still beat uncertified units. They suit shorter seasons.

howToChoose.note: Choose Most Efficient if the machine runs more than a few hundred hours a year, and standard certified otherwise.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A Most Efficient or Energy Star tier, an auto mode that cycles off and a hose drain. Set a target near 45 to 50 percent and let the machine cycle.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Uthfy 38 Pint is the whole-season pick, and the Ludatido 80 Pint is the pick for a large space you live in.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You run the unit for months every year. The Uthfy 38 Pint repays the premium in lower running cost.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: The unit runs only a few weeks a year. The Midea 22 Pint or Glowells 52 Pint is enough.

maintenance.why: A clogged filter forces the machine to work harder and erases the efficiency gain. Rinse and dry it fully.
Clean fins protect the efficiency rating that the Energy Star mark is based on. Use a soft brush.
A kink traps water and stops the unit. Keep a downhill run.
Blocked airflow raises the load and cuts efficiency. Keep a hand's width of space.
Built-in sensors drift about 5 percent. A separate meter prevents over-drying and wasted energy.

faq.q: Is an Energy Star dehumidifier worth it?
faq.a: For a machine that runs for months, yes. The efficiency gap compounds over hours, while for a few weeks of use it matters little.

faq.q: What is the difference between Energy Star and Most Efficient?
faq.a: Energy Star certifies models that beat a threshold. Most Efficient is a higher tier for the best performers in the category.

faq.q: Do stated savings percentages mean much?
faq.a: They compare against a baseline the maker chose. Use them as direction, and rely on the certification tier.

faq.q: Does a bigger unit cost more to run?
faq.a: In absolute terms it can, but it also cycles off sooner. A right-sized unit is efficient, and an undersized one runs nonstop.

faq.q: How long do these units last?
faq.a: Compressors typically last 5 to 10 years. Clean filters and coils help preserve efficiency.

Between 40 and 50 percent. Running below that wastes energy and dries the air, and a very low target forces the compressor to work longest in exactly the conditions where it removes the least water per kilowatt hour.
